work.title: Singegedichte an dem hohen Beylager Friedrichs Kronprinzens zu Dännemark und der Fürstin Louise Prinzeßin von Großbrittannien

history.p: The music to the cantata, which was composed in 1743 for the occasion of the marriage celebrations between Crown Prince Frederik and Princess Louise of Great Britain, has apparently been lost; only the text which Scheibe also wrote has survived. The performance took place at Christiansborg Palace on 11 December when the newly-wed couple had returned from Altona where they had stayed. During their visit they had often travelled to Hamburg visiting the Oper am Gänsemarkt which was patronised by, among others, members of the Danish court in Altona. Here they attended several operas lead by the impressario Pietro Mingotti and the troupe's musical leader Paolo Scalabrini. According to documents regarding the celebration in Copenhagen, Scheibe assembled a large orchestra not only including The Royal Orchestra but also the city wait and his assistants as well as servants and even singers from the Latin school, in all forty performers were engaged. Some of the rehearsals took place at Nytorv in Scheibe's private home and 24 music stands were therefore transported to his house. All the texts, including librettos to cantatas and dedicatory poems which were performed or recited at the event, appeared soon after in a printed collection including Scheibe's works as well as those by Thomas Clitau. The collection was published in instalments.

incipText.p: König! Wir danken vor dieses Ergetzen
So recht! erkennt ihr nun die Führung meiner Hand
Der Schäfer, wenn mein Arm ihn bindet
Wie schön vereinigt sich die Schickung und die Liebe!
Mir folgen Wonne, Scherz und Liebe
Die lockende Freude, das brünstige Scherzen
O König! dieses Fest dankt Dir Dein ganzes Reich
Es jauchzen die Völker, es scherzen die Felder

physDesc.watermark: two distinct watermarks are visible: 1) front pastedown, end pastedown and end flyleaf has an emblem consisting of the coat-of-arms with post horn on a cord, and 'D & C Blauw' beneath (Gravell:TJ162, TJ163, may be dated to the end of the eighteenth century; see also SchW B2:407); and 2) front flyleaf has the countermark 'C & I Honig'.
physDesc.physMedium: In 4o, title page (sig. [)(1r]), epigraph by Albrecht von Haller (sig. [)(1v]), list of characters and text (sigs. )(2r–)(6r), blank page (sig. )(6v); in all 12 pages.

Fairly thick paper; pages heavily trimmed affecting signatures, except title page. Work has later been rebound (possibly around 1800) with J.G.L. Aug. Vind, 'Bey Gelegenheit | Des Höchst=erpreislichen | Beylager=Festes' (Copenhagen: J.G. Höpfner, 1743; '5. Dec:' added in ink).
